+/**
+ * Shared helpers for filtering/classifying provider connections by their
+ * active/disabled state, independent of their last test result.
+ *
+ * A connection can have `isActive: false` (explicitly disabled by the user)
+ * while still carrying a stale `testStatus` of "active"/"success" from
+ * before it was disabled — callers that only filter on `testStatus` will
+ * incorrectly keep serving disabled connections.
+ */
+
+export interface ConnectionActiveFlag {
+  isActive?: boolean;
+  [key: string]: unknown;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Filters out connections that have been explicitly disabled
+ * (`isActive === false`). Connections without an `isActive` field are
+ * treated as active for backward compatibility.
+ */
+export function filterActiveConnections<T extends ConnectionActiveFlag>(
+  connections: T[] | null | undefined
+): T[] {
+  if (!Array.isArray(connections)) return [];
+  return connections.filter((connection) => connection?.isActive !== false);

Fixed in cbf73937c — good catch, and the extraction in this PR made it sharper: `filterUsableConnections()` reads `connection.testStatus` directly, so a nullish entry would have thrown `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null` at runtime.

Applied the explicit truthiness guard as suggested:
```ts
return connections.filter((connection) => !!connection && connection.isActive !== false);
```

Guarded by a regression test that fails against the previous `connection?.isActive !== false` predicate (verified failing-then-passing, per Hard Rule #18): `tests/unit/connection-status-filter-active-2526.test.ts` → "filterActiveConnections drops nullish entries instead of passing them through".
Addressed in 91c3c4469 — switched to `opts?.preserveCacheControl` so an explicit `null` argument no longer throws.

Good catch — addressed in 3316b755e. Added null/undefined object guards around `videos[0]` and `generatedSamples[0]` (and the nested `.video`) in `extractVideoFromResponse`, plus a regression test covering null/undefined/empty elements in both the documented and alternate Veo response shapes. A malformed upstream array now falls through to the explicit "no video" result instead of throwing.

Declining — this is a false positive. The current code typechecks cleanly:

```
$ npm run typecheck:core
> tsc --pretty false -p tsconfig.typecheck-core.json
exit=0
```

(Project is on TypeScript 6.0.3.) Since TS 4.9 the `in` operator narrows `unknown` properly: after `tool && typeof tool === "object" && "function" in tool`, the type of `tool` is `object & Record<"function", unknown>`, so `tool.function` is accessible without casting. See [microsoft/TypeScript#50666](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/50666).

Your suggested rewrite (`const t = tool as Record<string, unknown>`) is functionally equivalent at runtime but actually loses safety in two places: it casts the alias before checking `typeof t === "object"` against it, and it widens the function shape to `Record<string, unknown>` instead of letting the narrower type flow through. The original code is the more rigorous form.
